newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Beirut interim profits rise.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Beirut interim profits rise.

text.p: The Bank of Beirut reported on Monday big increases in assets, profits, customer loans and deposits in the half-year to June 1996 compared to first half of 1995.

The bank, which ranked 20th among Beirut's 82 banks in customer deposits in 1994, said in its unaudited January-June balance sheet that its assets rose 62 percent to 513 billion Lebanese pounds from 315.8 billion in June 1995.
Assets stood at 452 billion at the end of 1995.
Net income rose nearly 98 percent to 3.7 billion in June 1996 from 1.87 billion in June 1995. Net income was 4.3 billion at the end of last year.

Customer loans rose 71.6 percent to 187 billion from 109 billion and customer deposits rose to 415.5 billion from 246 billion -- a rise of 69 percent. Loans and deposits stood at 138 billion and 393.6 billion respectively at the end of 1995. Capital was 5.57 billion in June 1996 compared with 2.4 billion in June 1995, the bank said. The increase, through transfer from free reserves and retained earnings, was approved by a shareholders' meeting at June 2, 1995.

According to the Almanac of Lebanese banks, Bank of Beirut is owned by nine Lebanese investors, Saudi Prince Mohammad Bin Fahd al-Saoud and the Luxembourg-based holding company International Century Corporation.
It has 141 employees and nine branches in Lebanon.
